gap: Critic round 1 verdict, measured independently: PASS. Single largest remaining gap, one pass to fix: the DECISION path is the only write on this console whose affordance does not tell the truth before the click, and the only screen that makes a claim its own behaviour does not back. Two halves, same file. (1) POST /api/model/decisions is not stamped with can_edit, so VersionsPanel's 'Record a verdict' control renders enabled for a company viewer while both Train buttons two sections away render disabled with the wall's own Hebrew refusal. Measured live on an isolated instance with a real viewer session: header reads 'lachshbon tzfiya ein harshaat arikha' (the wall's sentence), both Train buttons disabled, and the Record control disabled=false. Worse, the refusal that actually lands after the click is NOT the sentence the console promises: the global middleware at kairos_api/auth.py:111 answers viewer writes first with the ENGLISH 'A viewer session is read-only.', measured by curl against POST /api/model/decisions and POST /api/model/training, while can_edit_reason carries the Hebrew wall string. tests/test_p7_can_edit.py asserts the stamp equals MODEL_WALL.reason(), which is self-consistent and does not prove parity with the body the write route really returns, so the test cannot catch this. (2) VersionsPanel.jsx's own header comment states 'Recording a ship verdict never copies an artifact. The form says so before the click, and the stored record repeats it afterwards.' Measured on screen: the form reads exactly 'the shipped model / Ship it / Do not ship it / Why / Record the decision / Cancel' plus the release-note rule when Ship is chosen, and carries no such sentence; DecisionRow renders an adoption line only when adoption.state is 'escalated', so a recorded ship verdict on the current model shows the single word 'Shipped' with nothing saying that nothing was copied, deployed or activated. The fix is one pass over kairos_api/model_console_api.py (stamp the decisions route), tv-break-dashboard/src/model/console/VersionsPanel.jsx (pre-disable the control, carry the refusal, print the no-copy sentence in the form and on a shipped record) and console-words.js. Minor, not blocking: the four header count chips are plain spans while the same four counts one screen below are working filters, so a number in the header opens nothing; and the console never states that placebo_correction_active and interval_calibration are method defaults rather than gates, which is why 13 and not 15.
history: critic round 1 (blind, did not build it): all four bars measured independently against a private instance on port 8085 with the auth store and the releases store both relocated to scratch, so no repository file changed (models/releases md5 identical before and after). STOPWATCH JS-16, target 120 s, baseline 'cannot start': console open with all 13 gates on screen 54 ms after one click, coverage 51 ms, drift 52 ms, training panel 52 ms, Train pressed to the new run visible as running 61 ms, run finished on screen unattended 9.09 s (the 1500 ms watch works, no manual refresh), versions to a recorded no-ship verdict visible 159 ms. Nine clicks, four screens, zero dead ends, about 9.5 s of app time of which 9.1 s is the training run itself. A/B against TensorBoard 2.18.0, which I launched myself on my own port over three scalar runs: the reference has no gate, no bar, no reason, no way to start a run and no way to record a verdict, so JS-16's central question is unanswerable there at any time budget; it wins only on interactive curve exploration, which a five-point weekly drift does not need. REGRESSION: 105 tests under the test_p7_ prefix pass (38 + 67, measured), all 8 audience gates in models/audience_model.json and all 5 retention gate families appear in the ledger, GET /api/impact still answers a channel account with the honest tri-state rather than a 403. LAWS: two figures traced byte for byte to the artifacts (first_break p=0.20341935034834022, n 476+816, and competitor_lineup held_out_delta_pct 2.162518438605128); zero rival channel names across all eight console payloads (coverage counts four channels and names only the operator's); every model route 403s for a channel account and the switcher does not render for one; zero em-dashes, en-dashes, emojis or exclamation marks and no file over 450 lines across every P7-owned source and test; the only hits for 'mishtamesh' are the verb 'mishtamshot' (runs use it), not the forbidden noun. Verified (2) was already fully built in an earlier round (per-gate 'what would end this' + earliest real date, confirmed live in browser, no code changed). All 105 tests under the test_p7_ prefix pass (was 101 across 12 files before this round, now 105 across 13; pytest --collect-only confirms). npm run build succeeds.
